title: Brewers Upset Defending Champions in NLCS Game 1 Rematch – MLB.com Exclusive
body:
Milwaukee’s postseason hopes were jolted into high gear on Tuesday night as the Brewers captured a 5‑2 victory over the defending champion Atlanta Braves, seizing Game 1 of the National League Championship Series and setting the tone for what could be a dramatically different chapter in the franchise’s modern era. Starting pitcher Brandon Woodruff delivered a masterful performance, allowing just two runs over seven innings while striking out nine, and the Brewers’ offense finally clicked after a sluggish regular season, generating timely hits that turned a tight early contest into a comfortable lead. The win not only gave Milwaukee a 1‑0 series edge but also signaled a shift in momentum that could reshape the narrative of a rivalry that began with the 2021 NLCS showdown.

The game’s early moments were a study in contrast. Atlanta’s ace, Max Fried, entered with the confidence of a defending champion, yet the Brewers’ lineup managed to scrape together three runs in the first two innings, courtesy of a two‑run double by outfielder Christian Yelich and a solo homer from catcher William Contreras. Fried, who had been dominant throughout the regular season, appeared unsettled, issuing two walks and conceding a crucial single that set the stage for the early deficit. Milwaukee’s defense, anchored by third‑base veteran Josh Bell’s flawless glove work, kept the Braves from capitalizing on their few opportunities, preserving the Brewers’ advantage.

Woodruff’s poise on the mound was the centerpiece of Milwaukee’s triumph. After a shaky start in the 2023 postseason that saw him surrender a three‑run inning in the NLDS, the right‑hander adjusted his pitch sequencing, leaning heavily on a sharpened cutter that baffled Atlanta’s hitters. He kept the Braves to just one run after the second inning, inducing two ground‑ball double plays that erased potential rallies. The veteran’s control was evident in his low walk total and his ability to locate the strike zone, a stark improvement from his earlier postseason outings. Behind him, the bullpen delivered a steady finish, with reliever Trevor Megill shutting down the final two innings without issuing a baserunner.

Beyond the box score, the victory carries broader implications for both clubs. For Milwaukee, the win validates the front office’s aggressive moves during the offseason, including the acquisition of veteran infielder Orlando Arcia and the promotion of young left‑hander Colin Rea, who provided depth throughout the regular campaign. The Brewers’ coaching staff, led by manager Craig Counsell, appears to have finally harnessed the team’s offensive potential, employing a more aggressive baserunning approach that paid dividends in the third inning when Ryan Braun’s stolen base set up a go‑ahead run. Conversely, the Braves must confront the reality that their championship pedigree does not guarantee success against a rejuvenated Brewers squad. Manager Brian Snitker will likely reevaluate his bullpen usage after Fried’s early exit and consider adjustments to his lineup to spark a more consistent offense, which has struggled to generate runs beyond the early innings throughout the series.

Analysts are already projecting a tightly contested series, with the Braves’ potent power core—featuring Ronald Acuña Jr., Ozzie Albies, and Austin Riley—still capable of turning games on a single swing. However, Milwaukee’s balanced attack, featuring a mix of seasoned veterans and emerging talent, could neutralize Atlanta’s firepower if they maintain the disciplined approach displayed in Game 1. The Brewers’ ability to execute in high‑leverage situations, especially with Woodruff setting the tone on the mound, will be a critical factor as the series shifts to Atlanta for Game 2.

Looking ahead, the Brewers are poised to ride the confidence generated by tonight’s performance into the next two games, where they will aim to extend their lead and force the Braves into a must‑win scenario. If Milwaukee can sustain Woodruff’s dominance and keep its offense clicking, the series could tilt in favor of a team that has long been labeled a perpetual underdog. For now, the victory serves as a statement: the 2024 NLCS may very well rewrite the narrative of a rivalry that began just three years ago, and the Brewers are determined to be the authors of its next chapter.
